name: Primary Cutaneous Gamma/Delta-Positive T-Cell Lymphoma
aliases: Primary Cutaneous Gamma Delta T-Cell Lymphoma

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: WHO-EORTC Classification for Primary Cutaneous Lymphomas

criteria.description: Presence of medium to large pleomorphic gamma/delta T-cells infiltrating the dermis and subcutis
Expression of T-cell receptor gamma/delta chains with absence of alpha/beta T-cell receptor expression
Presence of ulcerated plaques, nodules, or tumors primarily on extremities with aggressive clinical course
Exclusion of other cutaneous T-cell lymphomas such as mycosis fungoides and subcutaneous panniculitis-like T-cell lymphoma

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of gamma/delta T-cell infiltrate with supportive immunophenotyping and characteristic clinical presentation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires integration of clinical, histological, and immunophenotypic data due to overlap with other cutaneous lymphomas.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Ulcerated necrotic cutaneous plaques and nodules
Subcutaneous panniculitis-like infiltrates with gamma/delta T-cell predominance
searchTerms: deep skin inflammation with specific T-cells

common.symptomName: Systemic B symptoms (fever, night sweats, weight loss)
searchTerms: general body symptoms like fever and sweating

occasional.notes: Rare but reported in some cases

rare.symptomName: Neurological symptoms due to paraneoplastic syndromes
searchTerms: nerve symptoms from cancer-related immune effects
neurological signs due to paraneoplastic syndrome
nerve problems linked to cancer immune response

laboratory: Peripheral blood cytopenias in advanced disease
imaging: PET-CT showing hypermetabolic cutaneous and subcutaneous lesions
CT scan for lymphadenopathy and visceral involvement
genetic: Clonal rearrangement of T-cell receptor gamma genes
Absence of TCR alpha/beta expression confirmed by flow cytometry
other: Histopathology demonstrating epidermotropic and panniculitic infiltrates
Immunohistochemistry positive for CD3, CD2, CD56, and TCR gamma/delta

distinguishingFeatures: Better prognosis compared to gamma/delta lymphoma

redFlags: Rapid progression of ulcerated necrotic skin lesions
Presence of systemic B symptoms (fever, night sweats, weight loss)
Evidence of cytopenias or visceral organ involvement
references: Willemze R, Jaffe ES, Burg G, et al. WHO-EORTC classification for cutaneous lymphomas. Blood. 2005;105(10):3768-3785.
Swerdlow SH, Campo E, Harris NL, et al. WHO Classification of Tumours of Haematopoietic and Lymphoid Tissues. IARC; 2017.
Berti E, Facchetti F, Pileri SA. Primary cutaneous gamma/delta T-cell lymphoma: a review. Pathology. 2016;48(3):221-231.
